batch_strategy: Use matched condition-response experiments to localize recent failures, test unsupported predicted reversals, and extend sparsely measured retention curves. Prioritize labels that distinguish endpoint-specific solvent and loading relationships across recurring chemical families. All 32 IDs and their supplied premeasurement predictions are fixed together.

choices.reason: m174 at 100/1 and 100 uL fills the loading midpoint between 7f4f64cb791c71ba0420 and 36b45fbdbace5950c108. Their measured completion volumes differ by 25.20 mL. The predicted 27.38/44.49 mL tests whether that large association develops gradually or mainly at the largest loading.

m174 at 50/1 and 150 uL completes a ratio-by-loading comparison with measured low-loading 9c74e865c47b45a09229 and both 100/1 loading endpoints. This distinguishes a general high-loading completion increase from an interaction concentrated near 100/1.

m78 at 50/1 and 150 uL completes the loading series. Low- and middle-loading 2b97a1e0a6a4b944b760/61771d230b285babe4b6 measured decreasing onset but nearly identical completion. The current 49.40/90.61 prediction tests whether completion actually contracts at the highest loading.

m37 at 10/1 and 50 uL starts a matched loading pair around measured middle-loading 38e6b8bf0f089fcadd80. Its predicted 24.31/52.50 mL is close to the selected high-loading prediction, although the measured 20/1 loading series has a substantial onset decrease.

m37 at 10/1 and 150 uL completes that loading series. Comparison with 606886b17304ec494aa0, b6f1b33a5491968c645e, and 3b2c663a28a9f32bd1d3 at 20/1 identifies whether the onset-loading association emerges only as the eluent weakens or is being flattened by the predictor.

m82 at 5/1 and 150 uL completes a beta-ketoester loading series. Completion falls from 36.83 mL in low-loading 3ca8d2ff798fad4faffc to 29.34 in middle-loading f50c45b31cf41304c109. The predicted 30.73 mL tests a possible upturn versus continued decrease.

m58 at 2/1 and 100 uL tests an unsupported strong-eluent hump: its predicted 15.34/22.89 mL exceeds measured same-loading 10/1 response 04c495d5b53e3b1bceb7, 7.93/14.65. Together with the selected 5/1 row, this tests response placement for a sterically substituted phenol.

m58 at 5/1 and 100 uL completes that fixed-loading pair. The predicted 18.06/25.21 mL would create a pronounced maximum before measured 10/1 record 04c495d5b53e3b1bceb7. Measuring both ratios determines whether the model misplaced retention growth or a real local reversal occurs.

m208 at 1/1 and 100 uL tests the remaining predicted early-ratio hump, 8.70/14.05 mL, between measured pure-EA a8ad1c1e7d0c3c312f29 and 2/1 f525413ea8aed78db62a. The previous pure-EA reversal was rejected; this label checks whether the artifact persists at the intervening ratio.

m71 at 5/1 and 100 uL establishes the first point of a fixed-loading 5/1-to-50/1 experiment. Existing e4a7e43d15fcdee2ba1d and e9aa21d2af3158cfa4f5 give early responses at other ratios and loadings. This adds a controlled reference for the poorly anchored long-chain dibromothiophene curve.

m71 at 50/1 and 100 uL completes that pair. Predictions fall from 3.29/11.94 at 5/1 to 0.82/7.31 mL here as eluent weakens. This untested decline and high CW distance justify measuring a low-polarity sulfur environment without assuming ordinary monotonic retention.

m3 at 5/1 and 100 uL predicts an onset of only 0.99 mL, below measured same-loading pure-EA 3bb1d388702c98c505de and 20/1 c25aed72c162a62800ce. One label directly tests this deep predicted trough in a donor-free, highly aromatic structure.

m23 at 2/1 and 50 uL predicts V1/V2 of 8.11/7.23 mL. Measured same-loading 1/1 and 50/1 records 2928443b881ac6713786/96840797cfdea44e1467 have positive intervals. The label can identify which endpoint needs repair in this bulky acrylate's missing response region.

m48 at 50/1 and 100 uL also predicts inverted endpoints, 5.52/4.98 mL. Middle-loading pure-EA adbaa4b00d492d64eed5 and the 10/1 loading references 2f03edb1177fc5048002/7aebc58989fa288b11fc have positive intervals. This tests whether weak-eluent interval collapse is a model artifact in a distinct low-TPSA environment.

m130 at 1/1 and 50 uL starts a three-point fixed-loading nitrile response series. Its predicted completion, 14.50 mL, already exceeds measured same-loading 20/1 record b2ac848cc42390b01b9f. The strong side of this molecule's curve is currently sparsely anchored.

m130 at 5/1 and 50 uL tests the predicted completion maximum of 18.01 mL between selected 1/1 and 10/1 rows. Measuring the three ratios together separates an actual nonlinear response from unsupported extrapolation for 3,5-dimethylbenzonitrile.

m130 at 10/1 and 50 uL completes that series and connects it to measured 20/1 b2ac848cc42390b01b9f. Its predicted 7.00/14.04 mL implies completion decreases after 5/1 while onset rises. The label tests endpoint decoupling within a recurring aromatic nitrile family.

m84 at 20/1 and 50 uL bridges its sparse measured 10/1 anchor 331a940debe2ca50c35d to the selected 40/1 row. The predicted 6.62/15.83 mL tests where completion growth begins for ethyl para-chlorobenzoate under its recorded PE loading conditions.

m84 at 40/1 and the same loading completes that response pair. Its predicted 8.91/20.42 mL supplies a weak-eluent extension beyond 331a940debe2ca50c35d. This helps transfer across halogenated benzoates while retaining the loading differences from methyl ester record ede97e1f4b6e7fe9a7eb.

m56 at 50/1 and 150 uL tests loading transfer of middle-loading 5c11321c1ad5aec4ddf1, measured 7.03/23.27 mL. The predictor instead gives 8.51/21.05 here. Combined with the selected 100/1 extension, it distinguishes loading effects from further weak-eluent growth.

m56 at 100/1 and 150 uL completes a fixed-loading weak-eluent pair. Middle-loading 8d18a5b9f05363ff3a09/5c11321c1ad5aec4ddf1 localize substantial completion growth between 20/1 and 50/1. The predicted 9.76/24.45 mL tests whether that growth saturates or continues at higher loading.

m101 at 50/1 and approximately 150 mg loading, using 102.04 uL sample, tests transfer from approximately 100 mg record 2712213ca28bcadbfa61, measured 21.20/43.64 mL. Same-loading 10/1 anchor 987027dd660186de8266 helps distinguish a weak-eluent-specific loading association from a common offset.

m192 at 20/1 and 150 uL bridges same-loading 1/1 record 90b9bfcce4f713fc0a63 and new 50/1 record ad3ba40aa370443bc14f. The latter retained early onset with completion at 23.53 mL. This locates completion growth after the recent weak-eluent onset overestimate.

m156 at 20/1 and 150 uL tests loading transfer of the measured local onset maximum in 4cacfd98f3f85dc0dc0e. The current 8.55/15.89 mL prediction differs from its low-loading 10.16/14.10 response. This separates onset and completion associations in a zero-TPSA aromatic.

m99 at pure EA and 100 uL establishes a missing alpha-hydroxyester baseline below same-loading 1/1 and 2/1 records 36786ca0d1deaa0687ba/ad67d712133eac45ff64. The predicted 4.57/13.28 mL tests an onset change with almost unchanged completion relative to 1/1.

m182 at 5/1 and 100 uL starts a matched fluorenone pair. The model predicts onset rising to 9.21 mL here, then falling at 10/1. Measured 2/1 record 25d11f28e27e3f751324 and 50/1 record 76b4150b436d217e5b3e provide fixed-loading outer anchors.

m182 at 10/1 and 100 uL completes that pair: predicted onset falls to 6.15 mL while completion rises to 25.81. Low-loading 10/1 c9e08e156472783dee4e measured 4.88/26.63. The label distinguishes actual endpoint decoupling and loading response from a misplaced onset maximum.

m69 at 50/1 and 100 uL extends measured same-loading 20/1 a1089c52394c961fdb05 into an uncovered weak-eluent region. The predicted 8.18/20.66 mL can be compared with the selected longer-chain m70 and measured branched ketone 47b637b24c432172c8ed to learn side-chain-dependent response.

m70 at 50/1 and 100 uL predicts a smaller extension, 6.21/14.74 mL, than selected m69. Measured 20/1 loading brackets db4d7b947a514c78d89d/b6b5bac1327c9f0ca6fb provide references. The pair tests transfer across alkyl-chain environments with density differences retained.

m42 at 20/1 and 50 uL begins a matched weak-eluent pair for parent acetophenone. Same-loading 5/1 record 36919bba0092c5813f87 measured 8.68/14.10 mL. The current 10.74/16.73 prediction tests whether the parent curve grows only modestly before 50/1.

m42 at 50/1 and 50 uL completes that curve segment. Its predicted 12.82/22.68 mL contrasts with measured substituted ketones 92614816a3b3942bf123 and 6998dee6f6e69401798a. These labels anchor the unsubstituted parent without assuming substituent effects from polarity counts alone.

m20 at 2/1 and 100 uL fills the early response before measured 5/1 and 10/1 records c86b03e1b275528444a6/374b71ac526fe1051993. This ether-acrylate bridge tests transfer from phenoxy acrylate c11d5c3acbc28dddd0cf while retaining their different recorded loading solvents and densities.

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading associations depend on ratio, structure, and endpoint. The completed m135 10/1 and m37 20/1 series show appreciable onset decreases with much smaller completion changes. m78 also shows different loading associations for onset and completion. These observations do not establish a universal loading mechanism.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The predictor gives nearly flat loading responses in several missing series. Matched measurements can teach where this approximation holds and where endpoint-specific slopes change with solvent ratio.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m37 already show an onset-loading association at 10/1, does m78 completion contract at the largest loading, and does m82 completion continue decreasing at 5/1?

hypotheses.content: Weak-eluent benzoate responses require local ratio-by-loading and endpoint-specific relationships. m174's short 100/1 interval at low loading did not transfer to high loading: completion increased by 25.20 mL while onset increased by 4.07 mL. The relatively early m55 40/1 response and later m56 and m101 completion responses also limit a shared ester correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These are recurring ester environments with different onset and completion corrections. Loading midpoints, matched ratio extensions, and a sparse halogenated ester curve can constrain transferable relationships without imposing one family-wide offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does m174's completion increase emerge across loading and ratio, does m56 growth continue from 50/1 to 100/1, and does m101 retain its long completion at higher loading?

hypotheses.content: Solvent-response placement remains motif-specific and endpoint-specific. Recent m196 and m188 weak-eluent labels retained earlier onset than predicted, while m127's measured 5/1-to-10/1 completion increased instead of following the predicted reversal. Missing parent ketone, rigid ketone, side-chain ketone, and ether-acrylate curve segments need their own anchors.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controlled bridges can distinguish incorrect onset transitions from incorrect completion growth across carbonyl connectivity and substituent environments. This is more transferable than repeatedly correcting already anchored failure points.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is the predicted m182 5/1-to-10/1 onset decrease real, and do parent acetophenone and the longer-chain ketones follow their predicted weak-eluent growth?

hypotheses.content: For m156 at 50 uL, the measured 5/1 and 10/1 responses reject the earlier predicted onset dips. The new 20/1 label instead creates a local measured onset maximum, followed by earlier onset and longer completion at 50/1. The largest observed completion increase occurs between 20/1 and 50/1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This zero-TPSA example separates observed endpoint decoupling from previously rejected model artifacts. A loading contrast tests whether its local onset feature should propagate across the molecule's condition surface.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 20/1 onset maximum persist at 150 uL, or is it primarily associated with the low-loading record?

hypotheses.content: The inverted V1/V2 predictions for unmeasured m23 at 2/1 and m48 at 50/1 may reflect local model interval collapse. Nearby measured records for these molecules have positive intervals. The catalog also contains collapsed or inverted measured records elsewhere, so physical ordering is a useful prior rather than a sufficient label substitute.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These labels probe joint endpoint failures that quantile spans alone do not diagnose. They can identify whether onset, completion, or both need correction in two distinct low-polarity environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do these two candidate conditions have positive measured intervals, and which predicted endpoint accounts for any discrepancy?

hypotheses.content: Strong-eluent completion tails remain structure-local. m208's measured pure-EA and 2/1 responses reject its previous predicted pure-EA reversal, whereas m197 retains a longer pure-EA completion response. Current m208 1/1 and m58 2/1–5/1 humps remain untested model behavior; m99 needs a separate alpha-hydroxyester baseline.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Strong-side anchors can prevent valid local donor-associated tails from spreading to other structures and reveal whether fitting a measured point merely relocates an unsupported response hump.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the remaining m208 and m58 strong-side humps measured features, and does m99 pure-EA completion remain close to its 1/1 completion?

hypotheses.content: For m130, the predictor places relatively long completion in the sparsely measured 1/1–5/1 region, including a maximum near 5/1, despite measured 20/1 completion near 13 mL. This could be a real nonlinear response or an unsupported extrapolation. A fixed-loading series can distinguish these possibilities.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This tests an inadequately anchored aromatic nitrile response against better measured nitrile analogues, allowing substitution environment and conditions to matter beyond acceptor counts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50 uL, does completion follow the predicted approximately 14.5, 18.0, and 14.0 mL sequence at 1/1, 5/1, and 10/1 before meeting the measured 20/1 anchor?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest m61 measurements localize the earlier failure. Its 1/1 low-loading label was predicted closely, and both 2/1 labels were later than their acquisition predictions but differed only modestly across loading. The very large 50-versus-100 uL divergence at 5/1 therefore has limited support for transfer across ratios. The new m67 high-loading 5/1 label also did not reproduce that large divergence. With these comparisons now anchored, I shift acquisition effort to more discriminating remaining conditions.

The completed m135 and m37 series support decreasing onset with loading and smaller completion changes. m78's new 20/1 result extends its endpoint-specific loading association, although less strongly than at 50/1. These outcomes motivate testing response transfer across ratios and completing selected loading series, without assigning an unrecorded mechanism.

The largest recent completion failure was m174 at 100/1 and high loading: its acquisition prediction underestimated V2 by 22.91 mL. Its measured 32.72/61.66 mL response rejects transfer of the short low-loading interval to high loading. I select the missing loading midpoint and a same-high-loading 50/1 bridge. Meanwhile, m55 at 40/1 remained relatively early, m56 at 20/1 was earlier than predicted, and m101 at 50/1 exposed underestimated completion. These results strengthen the case for conditional ester response experiments.

The m127 ratio pair rejected its predicted completion reversal, and the m128 10/1 midpoint lay between its loading endpoints rather than below both. I reduce further sampling there. m208's pure-EA reversal was also rejected, but its current 1/1 prediction still warrants a direct test. For m156, the 5/1 dip was rejected and the new 20/1 onset maximum shows that rejecting a model dip does not justify imposing monotonic onset. Finally, the m196 and m188 weak-eluent labels exposed earlier onset than predicted; their outcomes guide restrained bridges and exploration of other missing carbonyl curves.
batch_rationale:
The batch combines recent failure repair with controlled exploration of uncovered condition-response relationships. The m174 comparisons locate a large completion failure in a ratio-by-loading surface. The m37, m78, m82, m101, and m156 choices test whether recorded loading associations persist, change direction, or affect only one endpoint. Density-times-sample-volume remains the loading amount; loading-solvent identity and volume are retained in every comparison.

Several acquisitions discriminate specific model behaviors: m58 and m208 strong-side humps, the m182 onset reversal, the m130 completion maximum, hydrophobic m71 and m3 troughs, and inverted endpoint predictions for m23 and m48. These are untested predictions. Matched pairs or short series make their labels interpretable even when the predictions prove approximately correct. Sparse m84, parent acetophenone, alkyl aryl ketones, and ether-acrylate conditions extend coverage within families represented throughout the catalog.

All 32 choices are distinct supplied candidates with new molecule-plus-condition tuples, and no selected tuples duplicate one another. Their molecules are already observed, so exploration focuses on missing structural-context-by-condition relationships. High CW distances support coverage for several choices, while matched contrasts provide the main justification for others. Single-predictor quantile spans are secondary evidence and are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. The expected benefit is improved joint V1/V2 generalization after retraining through better response placement, conditional loading relationships, and fewer unsupported local extrapolations.
